newsitem.title: USA: Britain's Spice Girls heat up U.S. music charts.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Spice Girls heat up U.S. music charts.

text.p: The Spice Girls, five women who have become the latest musical sensation in Britain, grabbed the number one spot on the U.S. singles charts, the group's label said on Wednesday.

Their song "Wannabe," which has already topped the charts in more than 30 other countries, ruled Billboard magazine's Hot 100 chart in its fifth week of release, said Virgin Records, a unit of EMI Plc. It ends the 11-week reign of Toni Braxton's "Un-Break My Heart."

Meanwhile, the Spice Girls' debut album "Spice" was the top-selling new entry in the week ended February 9, entering the U.S. album charts in sixth with sales of almost 82,000. It overshadowed new releases from California punk band the Offspring and Australia's teenaged hard rock trio Silverchair.
The U.S. singles chart is compiled from a sample of radio airplay and retail sales, while the album chart is based on sales data collected by SoundScan.
The number one album this week was No Doubt's "Tragic Kingdom," whose eight-week run at the top was ended the prior week with the release of the soundtrack to "Gridlock'd."

"Tragic Kingdom" sold about 119,000 copies in the latest week, taking its 58-week total to 5.3 million. "Gridlock'd" slipped to second with sales in the latest week of almost 94,000. Both albums are distributed by Interscope Records, an affiliate of Seagram Co. Ltd's Universal Music Group.

Braxton's "Secrets" rose two places to third with sales of just over 91,000, followed by the Warner Bros. Records soundtrack to "Evita" and Celine Dion's "Falling Into You," each down one. Braxton records for Arista Records, a unit of Bertelsmann AG and Dion records for Epic Records, a unit of Sony Corp. Warner Bros. is a unit of Time Warner Inc.
